transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. The main reason I’m here is that I'm really struggling at work lately. I manage health services, and anything that takes real, sitting-down brain work... it just feels like I hit a wall. 

Like, if I have to sit and do the monthly reports or plan out a big multi-site health event, I just keep putting it off. I know it matters, and I know I need to get it done, but I just avoid it. It's getting to the point where it's a real problem.
Have you struggled with this kind of difficulty focusing or avoiding tasks for most of your life, or is this a relatively new problem for you?

It's definitely not new. I've struggled with it for most of my life, honestly. 

Even way back in elementary school, my teachers would tell my parents that I was a bright kid, but I was just always daydreaming. I was constantly losing my worksheets, or I'd do the work and just... forget to turn it in. Really, the only way my homework ever made it to the teacher was if my mother physically checked my backpack every single night to make sure it was there. So, yeah, it's been going on for a long time.
Do you often feel physically restless, like you have a hard time sitting still or feel a need to be constantly moving?

No, not really. I mean, I can sit in a chair just fine without feeling like I need to get up or move around. It's... it's more like my mind is the thing that wanders off, not my body. So, no, I wouldn't say I feel physically restless like that.
When you are working on those tasks that require sustained mental effort, do you find that you make frequent careless mistakes because your attention drifts?

Yeah, I do. It happens more often than I'd like to admit. I'll be working on something like a clinic staffing schedule for work, or even just an email for my kid's soccer league, and I'll think I've checked it over. I'll hit send, and then... someone will point out that I put the wrong date, or I completely left off a location. Just... little details that I really should have caught, but my brain just sort of skipped over them.
Do you often find yourself forgetting to keep appointments, pay bills, or return phone calls in your day-to-day life?

Yes, I definitely do. I’ve been forgetting to return calls from volunteers, for example. And I'll end up missing small errands for events I'm supposed to be handling. It gets pretty embarrassing... once or twice I’ve actually had to apologize because a community meeting just completely slipped my mind. I didn't even realize I missed it until someone texted me to see where I was.
In your daily life, do you find that you are easily distracted by unrelated sights or sounds around you?

Yeah, definitely. It happens a lot at work. Like, I’ll be in a meeting, trying to listen to a budget update, and... if someone's phone vibrates on the table, or I hear people talking out in the hall, my attention just snaps right to that. 

Or it doesn't even have to be something I hear. Sometimes it's just my own thoughts—like I'll suddenly think about something I forgot to do for the soccer league. Whatever it is, it just pulls me completely away, and I'll suddenly realize I missed the last few minutes of what was actually being discussed in the room.

Are these difficulties with focus and organization present only at your workplace, or do you find that you struggle with them in other areas of your life as well, such as at home or in social situations?

It's definitely everywhere, not just at work. I mean, I’m still getting by at my job and with my community stuff, but... it's getting harder. People have had to step in and cover gaps for me when I drop the ball. I've let deadlines slip, and I’ve really embarrassed myself having to make these last-minute apologies to coworkers and friends. So, yeah, it's affecting pretty much all areas of my life right now.
To what extent would you say these challenges with focus and organization are currently interfering with your ability to maintain your professional responsibilities or your personal relationships?

Well, like I was saying, it's definitely interfering. I mean, I'm a health services manager, so I have a lot of responsibilities... and I'm still getting by, technically. But it's not smooth. At work, and with my community stuff, people have had to step in and cover gaps for me because I just lose track of things. Deadlines have slipped. And personally, it's just really embarrassing. I've had to make so many last-minute apologies to my coworkers and my friends because I forgot something or dropped the ball. It's definitely taking a toll.
